thread:
elaine (PM): Heads up — FinApps asked for a hard SLA: reduce tail latency on chat endpoint. They want P95 < 150ms for interactive sessions. This is customer-driven and could be a Dedicated upsell.
ben (Sales): Confirming — this is a pilot with a single product team, ~ $750k ARR potential if we hit it. They said current spikes kill UX.
samir (Eng): Quick thought: latency vs throughput trade here. We can chase kernel-level perf (big effort) or do workload shaping + prefix caching + routing to low-latency pool (smaller effort).
maria (ML): Also worth checking model sequence lengths and KV rehits. If they have long context, caching helps less. Can we get sample traces?
ej (SRE): We need an ops story: dedicated pool + autoscale headroom for spikes. SLA will need reserve capacity or a fallback. Also cost delta needs to be clear.
elaine (PM): Let's score this with a simple RICE-ish lens so leadership can decide. My initial back-of-envelope: Reach=1 (single customer), Impact=7 (high product impact for them), Confidence=6, Effort=8 (rough). Thoughts?
samir (Eng): I agree on Effort for kernel work. But split the scope: (A) low-effort: routing, cache toggle, RT prioritization (B) high-effort: operator/kernel + quantization. A could be 3 effort.
maria (ML): For Confidence, we should run a short measurement job on their session traces. If 70% of tokens are repeat prefixes, prefix cache will do most of the work. Confidence could move to 8 after that.
ben (Sales): From GTM POV, even a 60% improvement that we can guarantee as a contract hook is enough to close the deal. We don't need perfect micro-optimizations.
aj (SRE): Proposed launch criteria draft: 1) P95 < 150ms for their traffic slice for 7-day window; 2) <20% increase in per-request infra cost vs current; 3) automatic fallback to standard model on overload.
elaine (PM): Those look actionable. I'll write them into a short PRD but want engineering sign-off on feasibility/time.
samir (Eng): Feasibility notes: A (routing + cache flags) -> ~2 sprints across eng + ML infra. B (runtime kernels) -> 2-3 months. We can ship A as a canary.
maria (ML): Action: I'll run a 48h trace analysis and post numbers. If prefix hit rate > 40%, A is high ROI. Command I'll run: `curl -s -X POST https://telemetry/api/query -d '{"slice":"finapps-chat","range":"48h"}' | jq .summary`
elaine (PM): Ops-bot, can you create a ticket for the pilot and stub out the PRD checklist? :point_down:
ops-bot: Ticket created: PROD-1382 "FinApps chat latency pilot" — assignees: elaine, samir, maria — due: 2026-04-10.
aj (SRE): Quick risk callout: routing to a dedicated pool adds warmup time. We need pre-warm policy or a warm pool. That's extra infra cost.
samir (Eng): Agreed. For the canary we'll implement: `enable_prefix_cache=true`, `route_policy=lowlatency_pool`, and a conservative prewarm count. Small change set.
ben (Sales): I'll tell the customer we can commit to a pilot with those launch criteria and a report after the 7-day canary.
elaine (PM): Vote check — who supports prioritizing A (canary + routing + cache) in the next sprint? React with :thumbsup: if yes.
samir (Eng): :thumbsup:
maria (ML): :thumbsup:
aj (SRE): :thumbsup:
ben (Sales): :thumbsup: (will still push for timeline)
elaine (PM): Looks like it's green. Next steps: - Maria runs trace (48h) by EOD tomorrow - Samir & Aj scope work for a 2-sprint canary and post a short plan in #eng-runtime by Friday - Elaine drafts PRD and commit criteria, links ticket PROD-1382.
elaine (PM): Final note for prioritization doc: we'll record RICE as a table but treat this as a two-track project (A=fast follow, B=longer runway). Capture launch gating as a hard requirement for sales contract.
samir (Eng): If trace shows low prefix hit, fallback is to tune batching and tight routing SLAs. We'll report back with concrete numbers.
elaine (PM): Thanks all. We'll reconvene after Maria posts the trace. :v:
